originalTitle: Daniel Andrews’ government engaged in ‘concerning’ conduct but no evidence of firefighter union blackmail: Ibac report
summary: Anti-corruption watchdog’s long-awaited report finds ‘serious and concerning’ conduct by senior government members in dealings with union boss
content: Senior members of the former Daniel Andrews government engaged in “serious and concerning” conduct in their dealings with firefighters union boss Peter Marshall, a long-awaited report by the Victoria’s anti-corruption watchdog has found. The report by the Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission (Ibac) was tabled in parliament on Wednesday, some eight years after their investigation first began. While it did not find any individuals engaged in corrupt conduct, the report said senior members of the Andrews government engaged in “serious and concerning” conduct in their dealings with Marshall – the secretary of the United Firefighter Union (UFU) – when negotiating pay deals for the Country Fire Authority (CFA) and Metropolitan Fire Brigade (MFB), and their later amalgamation into Fire Services Victoria (FSV). This included “actions contrary to policy, procedure and codes of conduct, deliberate attempts to conceal and mislead, and the misuse of information.” Ibac also found the government made an “undisclosed deal” with Marshall, “to the exclusion of other key stakeholders,” which allowed him to “exert extraordinary influence over the negotiations” for both the CFA and MFB enterprise bargaining agreements. Marshall, meanwhile, was also granted “privileged access” to responsible ministers. The release of the report comes after years of legal attempts by the UFU to keep the it secret, including a high court challenge. The report said their investigation first began in 2018 following a tip-off that Marshall “blackmailed or otherwise compromised” Andrews “to change his position on the CFA EBA”. Ibac found no evidence of blackmail and did not substantiate the allegation, which both Andrews and Marshall denied. More to come.
chineseTitle: 丹尼尔·安德鲁斯政府从事“令人担忧”的行为，但没有证据表明消防员工会勒索：Ibac报告
chineseSummary: 反腐败监管机构期待已久的报告发现，高级政府成员在与工会老板打交道时的行为“严重且令人担忧”
chineseContent: 维州反腐败监管机构期待已久的一份报告发现，前丹尼尔·安德鲁斯政府的高级成员在与消防员工会老板彼得·马歇尔打交道时做出了“严重且令人担忧”的行为。独立广泛反腐败委员会 (Ibac) 的报告于周三提交议会，距其调查首次开始大约八年。虽然没有发现任何个人参与腐败行为，但报告称，安德鲁斯政府的高级成员在与联合消防员联盟（UFU）秘书马歇尔打交道时，在为国家消防局（CFA）和大都会消防队（MFB）谈判薪酬协议以及后来合并为维多利亚消防局（FSV）时，存在“严重且令人担忧”的行为。这包括“违反政策、程序和行为准则的行为，故意隐瞒和误导，以及滥用信息。” Ibac 还发现，政府与马歇尔达成了一项“未公开的协议”，“排除了其他主要利益相关者”，这使他能够“对 CFA 和 MFB 企业谈判协议的谈判发挥非凡的影响力”。与此同时，马歇尔还获得了会见负责部长的“特权”。该报告的发布是在 UFU 多年来试图通过法律手段保密（包括向高等法院提出质疑）之后发布的。该报告称，他们的调查于 2018 年首次开始，此前有举报称马歇尔“勒索或以其他方式妥协”安德鲁斯“以改变他在 CFA EBA 上的立场”。伊巴克没有发现勒索的证据，也没有证实这一指控，安德鲁斯和马歇尔都否认了这一点。未来还会有更多。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
